sections.html:
The counter is at 602 Anne Street in Jacksonville. Mail goes to a different spot, 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the main number is 910-347-3451.

Recording opens at 8 in the morning and the last item goes in at 5:30 in the afternoon, Monday to Friday. Marriage licenses stop a quarter hour earlier. Call before a long drive if weather or a holiday could change the schedule.

  • Walk-in address: 602 Anne Street, Jacksonville
  • Mailing address: 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville
  • Phone 910-347-3451, fax 910-347-3340
  • Weekdays only, 8 a.m. until 5:30 p.m.

sections.h2: How far back do Onslow County real estate records go?
sections.html:
Land records reach back to 1734. The office files conveyances, deeds of trust, cancellations of deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, separation agreements and road maintenance agreements.

Anything filed there is open to view at the counter. Staff will not fill in forms or search a title for you, because doing so would amount to practicing law without a license. Owners who want a title check should hire a closing attorney or order one through a title company.

You can also ask in writing to have a Social Security, bank or card number blacked out of an image on the county website. There is no charge for that request.

sections.h2: What to put on a deed before filing
sections.html:
Three things matter most: an excise tax statement, a tax certification form and clean personal data. Check each one before you present a deed.

  • Page one must show the excise tax, including a line for zero when nothing is due.
  • A tax-exempt transfer needs the legal reason for the exemption on page one.
  • A Tax Certification Form must be attached to the back of the original deed. That rule dates from July 1, 2013 and came from a decision of the Onslow County Tax Office.
  • Identity and account numbers stay out of the document unless the law or a court order requires them, or unless only the last four digits show.

Closing attorneys know these rules. A seller who prepares paperwork alone should phone 910-347-3451 first.

Beyond the state's uniform fees, Onslow County charges a few amounts of its own and accepts payment in specific forms.

Onslow County recording and payment rules
TopicRule or amount
Extra instruments in one document$10 for each additional instrument
Credit cardsAccepted for $5 or more, with a 3% processing fee added
Business checksPhysical address and phone number required
Personal checksAddress, phone, and driver license number with issuing state
Vital recordsCash or money order only
Plats18 by 24 inches, mylar or paper

The base fee for a general instrument under G.S. 161-10 is $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page. A deed of trust or mortgage runs $64.00 for up to 35 pages. Satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no fee. The latest fee schedule is linked from the county's Recording Information page.

sections.h2: When one package counts as several instruments
sections.html:
The office treats a package as several instruments when it holds two or more papers with different legal consequences or intent, each signed and acknowledged on its own and able to be recorded alone. The charge is $10 for each instrument after the first.

A seller sees this when a deed arrives bundled with a separate easement, a right-of-way agreement or a power of attorney in one stack. Each paper that could stand by itself is its own instrument. If you are unsure how many your package holds, ask the closing attorney or call 910-347-3451 before presenting it, because the extra charge is collected at the counter along with the base fee.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on an Onslow County house sale?
sections.html:
The seller does. The tax is $1 per $500, or part of $500, of the price or value conveyed, as set out in G.S. 105-228.

Payment goes to the register of deeds ahead of filing, and page one of the paper has to state the figure. Ask your closing attorney to add this tax to your payoff and other seller charges so your net sheet matches the check you receive.

Priority follows the clock. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, mortgage, option or lease longer than three years has no force against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is registered where the land lies.

A deed in a desk drawer protects nobody. In Onslow County, a judgment filed against a seller on Monday can beat a buyer whose deed reaches the office on Tuesday. Ask the closing agent for the recording time plus the book and page, and keep that confirmation with your sale papers.

Include an addressed, stamped return envelope with any mailed package so the original comes back to you. Make checks out to Onslow County Register of Deeds for the full amount.

Electronic plat submission through approved vendors began May 1, 2021, and plats can still be brought in. The county keeps the 18 by 24 inch statutory size. Sticky notes over wet-ink seals confuse the scanner, and residue gets a plat rejected. Anyone dividing a lot ahead of a sale should hand over a clean original.

Onslow grew 6.2% between the 2020 count and July 2025, reaching 217,175 people, with 91,470 housing units. Owners hold 63.7% of homes, the typical owner-occupied value is $236,400, and typical rent is $1,265. The county issued 1,372 building permits in 2025, so new construction competes with resale houses in many parts of the county. A seller near a new subdivision should expect buyers to compare the two.

sections.h2: Clearing liens before the deed goes in
sections.html:
Clear them first. Filing a lender's release costs nothing at this counter, so the only variable is how fast the lender sends it.

Property tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, so an unpaid bill follows the house to the buyer's closing. Ask the Onslow County Tax Office for the balance owed and have it paid from your proceeds. A seller whose debts exceed the likely price should talk to a closing attorney before choosing a date, since a recorded lien blocks a clean transfer. A cash buyer can still close quickly, but the same payoffs and releases are needed first. Collect the lender's payoff letter, the tax balance and a copy of your current deed, then hand them to the closing agent together so nothing waits on a missing paper. If your deed was recorded long ago, ask the office for a copy at the counter, where the records are open to view.

faqs.q: What is the street address of the Onslow County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 602 Anne Street, Jacksonville, NC. Mail is sent to 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the phone is 910-347-3451.

faqs.q: What time does the Onslow County Register of Deeds close?
faqs.a: Weekday recordings are accepted until half past five. The marriage license desk shuts 15 minutes sooner.

faqs.q: Does Onslow County add a card fee when recording?
faqs.a: Yes. Credit cards are accepted for payments of $5 or more, and a 3% processing fee is added to the total.

faqs.q: Will the Onslow County office help me fill in a deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot complete forms or run title searches, since they may not practice law. They can show you the public record.

faqs.q: What has to be attached to an Onslow County deed?
faqs.a: A Tax Certification Form goes on the back of the original deed. Page one must also show the excise tax amount, or the reason for any exemption.
